extracted.intended_audience: joint force commanders, combatant commanders, service component commanders, public affairs officers (PAOs), joint staff planners, and other DoD public affairs practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Doctrine and guidance for public affairs (PA) support during joint military operations, covering principles of information, PA functions, organization, media access/credentialing, relationship to information operations, OPSEC, planning, assessment, and resource requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information shall be made fully and readily available
rubrics_metrics.description: Information shall be made fully and readily available, consistent with statutory requirements, unless its release is precluded by national security constraints or valid statutory mandates or exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provisions of the Freedom of Information Act will be supported in both letter and spirit; requests for information from organizations and private citizens shall be answered quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free flow of information to Service members
rubrics_metrics.description: A free flow of general and military information shall be made available, without censorship or propaganda, to the men and women of the Armed Forces of the United States and their dependents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain internal information (command information) to create awareness, inform of significant developments, and enable Service members and families to serve as ambassadors for the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not withhold information to avoid criticism or embarrassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Information will not be classified or otherwise withheld to protect the government from criticism or embarrassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempting to deny unfavorable information or failing to acknowledge its existence leads to media speculation, perceptions of a cover-up, and lost public trust; difficult or unfavorable issues should be openly and honestly addressed as soon as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withhold information only for security or safety/privacy reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Information shall be withheld only when disclosure would adversely affect national security or threaten the safety or privacy of the men and women of the Armed Forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions to withhold must be consistent with statutory limits and national security constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propaganda has no place in DOD public affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Propaganda has no place in DOD public affairs programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA activities must avoid censorship and propaganda and must focus on truthful, accurate information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell the Truth
rubrics_metrics.description: JFC PA personnel will only release truthful information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The long-term success of PA depends on integrity and credibility; deceiving the public undermines trust and support for the Armed Forces and PA activities. Accurate, balanced, credible presentation leads to confidence and legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide Timely Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders should be prepared to release timely, factual, coordinated, and approved information about military operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely release of truthful information helps frame public debate, supports decision-making, and counters adversary information initiatives. Delays increase the risk that adversaries become the preferred information source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice Security at the Source
rubrics_metrics.description: All DOD personnel are responsible for safeguarding sensitive information; as sources of information, each DOD member should be aware of OPSEC issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information must be approved for public dissemination before release; PA is the organization authorized by DOD for release to the public and bears key OPSEC responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide Consistent Information at All Levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders should ensure that DOD PA operations put forth a consistent message through its many voices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information should be appropriately coordinated and in compliance with official DOD and supported command guidance before release to the public to avoid mixed messages across levels of command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell the DOD Story
rubrics_metrics.description: Every military and civilian member of DOD should help provide accurate information about the Armed Forces and national defense operations to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders should educate and encourage personnel to 'tell the DOD story' by providing timely, appropriate information for public release; official spokespersons still must be designated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate PA into planning, training, and equipping at all levels
rubrics_metrics.description: PA operations must be integrated into all levels of command and incorporated into every phase of operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA personnel must be planned, trained, and equipped; PA should be incorporated in planning to anticipate external interest and be prepared to respond throughout the operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA supports the JFC by communicating truthful unclassified information
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission of joint public affairs is to support the JFC by communicating truthful and factual unclassified information about DOD activities to US, allied, national, international, and internal audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA organizations advise the JFC on media events and operations, assist development and dissemination of command information messages, help with INFOSEC and OPSEC by establishing ground rules for media coverage, and assist media understanding of military events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use PA to support command strategy and counter adversary propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: Public affairs counters adversary propaganda and disinformation by providing a continuous flow of credible, reliable, timely, and accurate information to military members, families, the media, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA must be engaged in operational planning, monitor domestic/international press and relevant intelligence, understand adversary propaganda techniques, and anticipate/counter propaganda by getting accurate information out first to set context and frame debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use public information as a deterrent and to shape perception
rubrics_metrics.description: PA should consider public information options to deter conflict and to put international public spotlight on issues; using truthful information to communicate US goals, expectations, and potential actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA may highlight deployments and force projection to show preparedness; such activities can influence adversary decision-making and public/coalition perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA and Information Operations must be coordinated but separate
rubrics_metrics.description: PA and IO activities must be aware of each other’s activities for maximum effect; efforts differ in audience, scope and intent, and must remain separate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure appropriate coordination between PA and IO consistent with DOD Principles of Information, policy/statutory limits and security. PA is not an IO discipline or PSYOP tool and should have no role in planning or executing PSYOP or MILDEC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate PA statements/releases with MILDEC
rubrics_metrics.description: PA activities affect, and are affected by, military deception (MILDEC) operations; PA statements and releases must be coordinated with MILDEC to ensure deception plans are not revealed or compromised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA must be aware of MILDEC operations but must not plan or execute them.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAOs are the principal spokesperson and senior advisor to the JFC
rubrics_metrics.description: The public affairs officer (PAO) is the JFC’s principal spokesperson and senior advisor on public affairs, on the commander’s personal staff and directly responsible for all the JFC’s PA requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs must have the ability to provide information to the media, the commander, and supporting forces in near real time and provide oversight of subordinate JIB(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Information Bureau (JIB) director responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The JIB director, with supporting JIB staff, is responsible for coordinating all media operations within the operational area and provides and coordinates support to the JFC through the joint force PAO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The JIB serves as a logistic and information base for media relations operations and may issue credentials and ground rules tailored to the operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credentialing and media access criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The criteria for credentialing journalists are established by the joint force PAO or the JIB director; credentialing is primarily a method of validating individuals as journalists and providing them with information that enhances their ability to report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credentialing is not intended to be a control measure but ensures official status under the Geneva Conventions in the event of capture. Commanders should not provide information to non-credentialed, unregistered journalists without guidance from the joint force PAO or the JIB director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitate media access to US forces
rubrics_metrics.description: The JFC must organize for and facilitate access of national and international media to US forces, including those engaged in combat operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media access shapes public perception; commanders should expect journalists in operational areas, some of whom will embed with units; JIB should provide support (equipment, transport, communications) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA has three basic functions
rubrics_metrics.description: PA has three basic functions: public information, command/internal information, and community relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each function plays a role in joint operations and will vary with mission. Public information focuses on media relations; command/internal information focuses on informing internal audiences; community relations supports civil-military ties in home station communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA program responsibilities (media relations, plans/logistics, internal info, community relations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each JFC’s PA program includes responsibilities to conduct media relations, plans and logistics, command/internal information, and community relations, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA program structure and emphasis will vary by operation; ensure plans and logistics support media and internal communications requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess PA effectiveness by media tone, products, polls, and internal feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate PA success and credibility by assessing the general tone of the media, continuous assessment of available media products and public opinion polls, and estimating impact on internal audiences via feedback from other functional areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA personnel should monitor impact of news coverage on the mission and host nation concerns and use these measures for continuous assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA provides trusted counsel and analysis to leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: PA provides trusted counsel to leaders, including analyzing and interpreting the global information environment, monitoring public understanding, forecasting impact of operations, and preparing JFCs to communicate with audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA should translate media and intelligence inputs into actionable advice for commanders and planning staffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA enhances morale, readiness and public trust
rubrics_metrics.description: PA enhances morale and readiness by informing personnel and families and fosters public trust and support by building understanding of military roles and missions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective PA supports recruitment, training, and sustainment by maintaining public backing and congressional support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for information shall be answered quickly
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for information from organizations and private citizens shall be answered quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness is part of DoD's responsibility to make accurate information available so the public, Congress, and news media may assess and understand facts about national security and defense strategy.
